title: Russian woman detained after Moscow car bombing injures aide to pro-Kremlin Ukrainian politician | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Russian authorities said on Monday they had detained a young Russian woman in connection with a Moscow car bombing last week that injured a former aide to a pro-Kremlin Ukrainian politician.

Sergey Zavorotny, who served as an adviser to Mykola Azarov, Ukraine’s former pro-Russian prime minister,was severely injuredin Friday’s attack and taken to a Moscow hospital for medical care, authorities said.

Azarov served as the Ukrainian prime minister from 2010 to 2014, when he fled to Russia during street protests that became known as theMaidan Revolution.

Russia’s security agency FSB said it had detained the woman, born in 2005, in connection with the attack on Zavorotny’s car, according to Russian state news agency RIA Novosti.

The FSB alleged she carried out the attack “on the instructions of Ukrainian special services,” RIA reported. Ukraine made no immediate comment on the allegations.

Video from the scene on Friday showed a dark gray SUV that had been heavily damaged, with the windows apparently blown out.

The FSB claimed the woman had been “psychologically manipulated” since July by “a representative of a fraudulent call center” posing as a Russian Central Bank employee into transferring a large sum to so-called “safe accounts,” which was then used to further pressure her.

CNN cannot independently verify the FSB’s claims.

The allegationsfollowa pattern of attacks across Europe in which authorities have said individuals were manipulated or recruited online to carry out acts of sabotage, including arson.

Friday’s car bombing was the second apparent assassination attempt inside Russia in the space of two days. On Thursday, a car explosion in St. Petersburg killed a Russian serviceman, the local Investigative Committee said.

The incidents come amid renewed US efforts to end the war in Ukraine. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Russia’s Vladimir Putin last week after US-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi concluded with no clear breakthrough.
